Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Is the Quran just rules, or care for the weak?

What the Quran says of the orphan, the hungry and the daughter. What it commands, and what historians debate.

Part 1 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ١ فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ٢ وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? For that is the one who drives away the orphan And does not encourage the feeding of the poor.

Quran · Al-Ma'un 107:1-3

Translation

But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into your hand. You help the victim and the fatherless.

Original · Hebrew

רָאִ֡תָה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה ׀ עָ֘מָ֤ל וָכַ֨עַס ׀ תַּבִּיט֮ לָתֵ֪ת בְּיָ֫דֶ֥ךָ עָ֭לֶיךָ יַעֲזֹ֣ב חֵלֶ֑כָה יָ֝ת֗וֹם אַתָּ֤ה ׀ הָיִ֬יתָ עוֹזֵֽר׃

the Psalms · 10:14

World English Bible

﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ٩ وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ١٠﴾

Translation of the meaning

So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]. And as for the petitioner,[1942] do not repel [him].

Translator's notes

[1942] Anyone who seeks aid or knowledge.

Quran · Ad-Duha 93:9-10

Translation

If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two. Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον· καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετʼ αὐτοῦ δύο. τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:40-42

World English Bible

Start with a surprise. A short chapter asks about the person who denies the judgment, and describes him not by what he says but by what he does: he pushes the orphan away and does not urge feeding the poor. Another passage tells the hearer to treat the orphan gently and not to scold the one who asks. One test the book sets for sincerity is how you treat those who can do nothing for you.

A question for you

Which do you think shows a person's character better?

If you sayWhat they say they believe.
ThenWords matter, and the chapter does not dismiss them. It simply adds a second witness: what a person does.
If you sayHow they treat those who cannot repay them.
ThenThat is the test the chapter itself puts.
If you sayBoth together.
ThenThat is close to what the passages ask: belief and care held together, not one in place of the other.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَيُطْعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا٨ إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَآءً وَلَا شُكُورًا٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they give food in spite of love for it[1813] to the needy, the orphan, and the captive, [Saying], "We feed you only for the face [i.e., approval] of Allāh. We wish not from you reward or gratitude.

Translator's notes

[1813] The meaning here may also be "out of love for Him," i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

Quran · Al-Insan 76:8-9

Translation

It is well with the man who deals graciously and lends. He will maintain his cause in judgment. For he will never be shaken. The righteous will be remembered forever. He will not be afraid of evil news. His heart is steadfast, trusting in Yahweh. His heart is established. He will not be afraid in the end when he sees his adversaries. He has dispersed, he has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever. His horn will be exalted with honor.

Original · Hebrew

טֽוֹב־אִ֭ישׁ חוֹנֵ֣ן וּמַלְוֶ֑ה יְכַלְכֵּ֖ל דְּבָרָ֣יו בְּמִשְׁפָּֽט׃ כִּֽי־לְעוֹלָ֥ם לֹא־יִמּ֑וֹט לְזֵ֥כֶר ע֝וֹלָ֗ם יִהְיֶ֥ה צַדִּֽיק׃ מִשְּׁמוּעָ֣ה רָ֭עָה לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א נָכ֥וֹן לִ֝בּ֗וֹ בָּטֻ֥חַ בַּיהוָֽה׃ סָמ֣וּךְ לִ֭בּוֹ לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־יִרְאֶ֣ה בְצָרָֽיו׃ פִּזַּ֤ר ׀ נָ֘תַ֤ן לָאֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים צִ֭דְקָתוֹ עֹמֶ֣דֶת לָעַ֑ד קַ֝רְנ֗וֹ תָּר֥וּם בְּכָבֽוֹד׃

the Psalms · 112:5-9

World English Bible

Here the givers speak to the one they feed: we feed you for the sake of God, and we want neither reward nor thanks. The hungry person is not made to owe anything. This is a picture of giving that protects the dignity of the one who receives before it fills the hunger. The book puts the poor person, the orphan and the captive side by side in it.

A question for you

What makes help feel like a gift and not a debt?

If you sayThat the giver does not wait to be thanked.
ThenThat is the picture in the passage: giving that asks for neither reward nor thanks.
If you sayThat the giver does not tell anyone.
ThenQuiet giving does protect dignity. The passage goes further and asks that the giver want nothing back at all.
If you sayThat the receiver can give something back one day.
ThenA real human hope, and good between equals. The passage describes giving where no return is expected.

﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُۥدَةُ سُئِلَتْ٨ بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍ قُتِلَتْ٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

Translation of the meaning

Translation

As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?”

Original · Ancient Greek

Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσδραμὼν εἷς καὶ γονυπετήσας αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσω ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;

the Gospel (Mark) · 10:17

World English Bible

﴿وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِٱلْأُنثَىٰ ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُۥ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ٥٨ يَتَوَٰرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ مِن سُوٓءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِۦٓ ۚ أَيُمْسِكُهُۥ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ ۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ٥٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when one of them is informed of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief. He hides himself from the people because of the ill of which he has been informed. Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:58-59

Now the hardest case. One passage pictures the girl who was buried alive being asked, on the Day, for what wrong she was killed. She is the one asked, as if she had a voice and a right to an answer. Another passage forbids killing children out of fear of poverty and answers the fear: provision comes from God, for them and for you. A third describes a father's shame at news of a daughter.

A question for you

What does it change when the child is the one who is asked?

If you sayIt gives the child a voice.
ThenYes. The picture makes the child a person with a claim, not a burden.
If you sayIt moves the question from fear to responsibility.
ThenThat is the movement across the passages: the fear is named and answered, and the responsibility stays.
If you sayI find this passage very hard to read.
ThenMany do. It is meant to be felt. You can stop here and return another day.
